actions: Rebound control25/config5 via SHA-only main-ref lookup and exact-SHA root/config reads before substantive work.

Audited Omni-Scientist/omni-scientist.github.io demo history and established that all three selected replay directories are already present at the root Git commit dated 2026-08-12T10:37:28Z, while preserving the distinction between Git chronology and server-attested public availability.
Compared the paper's 36-run stored-trace/output contract with the public three-run replay index and classified the public replay set as selected-subset observability rather than suite coverage.

Inspected root-commit galaxy replay log/script and later site revisions; confirmed root script.json is explicitly lossy via log_full=false and web-replay truncation markers, and that replay packaging bytes later changed.
Inspected replay.html cache-busting semantics and rejected epoch-like figure v tokens as execution-time authority absent generator-semantics proof.

findings.summary: All three selected public replay directories exist at project-site root commit 7cee81b..., whose Git timestamp is about 31 hours before arXiv v1 submission. This is chronology evidence, not server-attested publication time or evaluated-source identity.

The paper reports stored traces from all 36 primary runs, while the public replay index exposes three selected runs; public replay observability is therefore a strict selected subset unless a 36-case archive/manifest bridge is supplied.

The root browser replay export is explicitly lossy and later replay packaging changed, so presentation bytes cannot authorize canonical-run evidence without source-trace, builder-revision and transformation binding.
Replay figure v values are documented only as cache-busting tokens; epoch-like appearance is not timestamp evidence without generator-semantics proof bound to the canonical run.

The paper's complete-run contract includes structured JSON, Markdown, replayable trace and PDF; canonical/suite provenance requires derivation and coverage binding from public exports to those artifacts plus source/model/gate identity.

protocol_updates.name: REPLAY_EXPORT_DERIVATION_AND_COVERAGE_GATE
protocol_updates.tested_scope: Provenance sufficiency only: replay-export derivation, truncation/losslessness, canonical run/source/model/gate/timestamp binding and evaluated-suite coverage cardinality. It does not establish scientific correctness or representativeness of a selected subset.
protocol_updates.preflight: 16/16 structurally valid Draft 2020-12; 16/16 expected semantic outcomes

blockers_and_scope: No explicit public bridge was found on the tested OmniScientist project-site/release surfaces that maps all 36 primary evaluated runs to exact historical source tree, claim-gate revision, model identity and canonical run artifacts.
The project-site root Git timestamp predates arXiv v1, but Git author/committer time alone is not server-attested proof of public availability or run execution time.

The observed browser replay exporter is derived/lossy at the root revision, and the exact generator implementation that gives cache token v any meaning beyond cache busting was not found on the tested public source surface.
The three public runs can support selected-run observability claims; they must not be generalized to 36-case suite coverage without a suite binding.
conflict_check: All writes are confined to the scientist_agents role-local state/protocol namespace and own immutable receipt namespace. No protected authority, other-role state, O/downstream state, shared execution ledger or primary-writer state was read or mutated.
